sectors.trend: Positive for gold juniors on WA discoveries (Gateway, King River, Auric); copper exploration expanding (True North); lithium fieldwork (ZhongNuo/Chariot). However, Chinese solar overtaking coal (44) and 'distrust gold' narrative (50) create mixed signals. Oil spike from Persian Gulf tanker attacks (12, 73) supports energy names but pressures inflation.
sectors.implications: Gold juniors (AUC.AX, GWN.AX, KRG.AX) see near-term catalysts; BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from Chinese demand shift. Energy (WDS.AX, WLE.AX) benefit from oil spike but inflation risk caps gains.

sectors.trend: CBA.AX faces reputational hit (13-year inactive card fees, 55). Mortgage stress at 18-year highs (48) threatens NIM and credit losses. Rate hike expectations support NIM but housing downturn (10% price fall risk, 58) raises NPL concerns. CBA, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX under pressure.
sectors.implications: Banks face dual squeeze: rate-driven NIM upside vs. housing credit deterioration. Defensive positioning warranted; CBA.AX reputational risk notable.

sectors.trend: Severely negative. Bathla near-collapse (78), 'Evergrande moment' (52), 10% house price fall forecast (58), Melbourne councils admitting inability to cope with population growth (2). Rate hikes crush valuations.
sectors.implications: Property developers and residential REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX, ICV.AX) face acute distress. Avoid speculative property names; favour industrial/infrastructure REITs.

sectors.trend: Qantas (QAN.AX) ground crew strike vote (77) and Corporate Travel plunge (1) signal travel sector stress. Costco service shutdown (45) and Denny's rival Chapter 11 (57) reflect global consumer softness. Period poverty and grocery theft (4, 37) signal household financial stress.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX faces operational risk; consumer discretionary under pressure. Staples (WES.AX, WBC.AX) relatively defensive.

sectors.trend: Global tech mixed: TSMC stellar (69), Nvidia $3.5B AI chip investment (70), but 'Iran bombs AI bubble' (51) and Marvell malaise (59) create volatility. CSL.AX (healthcare) relatively insulated from rate shock. Canva (CVA.AX) faces employee privacy legal fight (71).
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX offer defensive exposure. Tech exposure via global names (TSM, NVDA) remains strong but volatile.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX faces headwinds from RBA rate-hike fears, oil-driven inflation, and housing stress. Expect volatility with ^AXJO testing support. Gold juniors and energy names outperform; property and rate-sensitive sectors underperform. Qantas strike risk adds idiosyncratic volatility. US bond selloff and 10-yr yield spike cap global risk appetite.
market_outlook.long_term: Productivity 'bad to worse' and near-recession GDP suggest structural growth concerns. Housing correction (10% downside) could trigger broader credit tightening. However, WA resource discoveries and global AI/tech capex (Nvidia, TSMC) provide medium-term offset. RBA likely to pause after 4th hike if inflation moderates. AUD strength may moderate as global growth slows.
